what: The BMI Calculator works out your Body Mass Index from your weight and height. It shows your BMI number, the standard category for adults, and the healthy weight range for your height. You can use metric units (kg and cm) or imperial units (lb, feet and inches).

BMI is a quick screening number that doctors and health websites often use. It can help you understand where you stand and set a sensible goal, but it does not measure body fat directly and does not account for muscle, age or body type.
The calculation runs in your browser and your numbers are not sent anywhere. Results are estimates and not medical advice; talk to a doctor about your health.
uses: Get your BMI and category in a few seconds.
See the weight range that gives a BMI from 18.5 to 24.9 for your height.
Check your BMI again after a change in weight.
Use kg and cm or lb, feet and inches, whichever you know.
See which range your number falls into.
tutorial: In "Units", choose "Metric (kg, cm)" or "Imperial (lb, ft, in)". The weight label and height boxes change to match.
Type your weight in the "Weight (kg)" or "Weight (lb)" box.
For metric, type your height in "Height (cm)", for example 175. For imperial, type feet in "Height (ft)" and inches in "Height (in)", for example 5 and 7.
"Your BMI" shows the number with 1 decimal. "Category" shows Underweight, Healthy weight, Overweight or Obese.
"Healthy weight for your height" shows the weight range for a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9, in kg or lb depending on your units.
features: BMI = weight in kg ÷ (height in meters × height in meters). Imperial values are first changed to kg and meters (1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, 1 inch = 0.0254 m).

Below 18.5 is Underweight, 18.5 to under 25 is Healthy weight, 25 to under 30 is Overweight, and 30 or more is Obese. The category follows the BMI shown with 1 decimal, so 24.96 (shown as 25.0) is Overweight.
Lowest weight = 18.5 × height²; highest = 24.9 × height². Shown to 1 decimal in kg or rounded to whole pounds.
Switch units at any time; the right boxes appear automatically.
The numbers update as you type.

example.title: Worked example: metric and imperial
example.text: You weigh 70 kg and are 175 cm tall. Your height is 1.75 m, so BMI = 70 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 22.9 and the category is "Healthy weight". The healthy range shows 56.7 – 76.3 kg. In imperial, a person who weighs 160 lb and is 5 ft 7 in tall gets a BMI of 25.1, "Overweight", with a healthy range of 118 – 159 lb. This is only a screening result, not a diagnosis.

tips: Weigh yourself at the same time of day for a fair comparison.
In imperial mode, put whole feet in the ft box and the rest in the in box; 5 ft 7 in, not 67 in the feet box.
Muscular people can get a high BMI without having extra fat.
These adult categories do not apply to children or teens, who use age-based charts.
Use BMI together with other checks, like waist size, and ask a doctor for advice.
problems: Enter both a weight and a height above 0.
My BMI is very high or very low
Check the units. Typing pounds while "Metric" is selected, or meters instead of cm, gives wrong numbers.
Changing "Units" switches between the cm box and the ft and in boxes. Type your height again in the new boxes.
I am fit but the category says Overweight
BMI does not separate muscle from fat. Talk to a health professional for a fuller check.
